findings.issue: Workspace line coverage is 90.08%, below the 91.48 baseline. This is a 1.40 point drop with sc-jev-py excluded (see evidence). Per-crate lines: sc-agent-http 92.30 (695/753); sc-jev 78.94 (356/451); sc-jev-backends 87.76 (516/588). Baseline per-crate figures were not supplied. The earlier sc-jev-backends figure of 91.48 is from a stale file of unknown origin and is not a trustworthy comparison.

Within sc-agent-http, transport.rs (66.7%), redact.rs (80.0%) and test_util.rs (82.2%) have the lowest coverage.

findings.issue: The two exhaustion errors (all sends used, 90 s budget spent) share NetworkErrorKind::Busy and differ only in detail text ("N sends exhausted" vs "retry budget exhausted"). A caller can tell them apart only by string matching.
findings.recommendation: Acceptable if the spec only requires distinguishable messages (tests assert both). If callers must branch on the cause, add a distinct kind or a typed field.

review_results.retry_numbers: Correct. Backoff is 1/2/4 s (tests assert 1,2,4,8,16,30,30,30). Retry-After is clamped to 30 s. The parser is integer-only, with 32-byte and 32-digit saturation; the cases cover sign, exponent, inf, NaN, an HTTP-date, 33 bytes, empty, '1.', '.5' and '1.2.3'. Jitter is bounded to 250 ms in production (hash % 251) and in the test hook (jitter.min(250 ms)).
review_results.budget_semantics: Matches the stated assumption. The budget is checked only after a busy reply and before waiting. The wait is min(base + jitter, remaining), so a capped wait ending exactly at 90 s goes straight to the next cancel check and send, with no second budget check. The 120 s in-flight request timeout is documented as outside the budget.
review_results.cancel: Checked before each attempt and between wait slices of at most 100 ms (WAIT_SLICE). A cancel during an in-flight request is seen only when it returns, and this is documented.
review_results.redaction: send_with_busy_retry applies redact() in a single map_err over the whole retry_loop, so every Err path is covered, including errors from third-party Transport impls. send_and_parse also redacts errors from parse.
review_results.agent_reuse: UreqTransport builds one agent in new() and clones share it. The test test_agent_is_reused_across_sends exists and passes.
review_results.loopback_https_only: loopback_for_tests and Endpoint::loopback_http are gated on feature test-util. Production UreqTransport refuses non-https with a Tls error (test_release_build_refuses_http passes). The test-util absence gate is clean.
review_results.body_cap: 8 MiB cap is applied while streaming via take(cap+1) for all statuses, 200 and 500 included. Over-cap returns response_invalid. test_response_body_cap_is_8_mib_while_streaming passes.
review_results.secret_single_site: expose() (ureq_transport.rs, #[expect(clippy::disallowed_methods)]) is the only ResolvedApiKey::as_str call, and SecretHeader::matches goes through it.
review_results.panics: No unwrap, expect or panic in library paths. The only unreachable! is retry.rs:172, a hook/start mismatch that is a programming error and cannot happen across public APIs. The remaining expect calls are in tests.
review_results.test_determinism: The retry tests use FakeClock, RecordingSleeper and fixed jitter, so nothing sleeps. The loopback tests passed in 7 runs total (1 + 6 loops) with no failures. test_timeout uses a real 1 s stall.
